messages:
rachel: Quick triage — seeing a small P50 regression on host preparse after yesterday's kernel-picker rollout. Median latency for small requests went from ~6.2ms -> ~7.6ms. Uploading traces.

matt: I see it on our canary too. Flamegraph points to host_tokenizer::tokenize_v2 as the hotspot, ~0.9ms extra. KV cache hit-rate looks steady.

anjali: Wasn't the kernel affinity change the one that adjusted min-batch from 2 -> 4? Could that increase fragmentation for short seqs?

rachel: Exactly. Kernel picker now prefers qint8 kernels on A100 for tiny batches. Traces show an extra memcpy during proto-unpack on the host path.

kai: Dug into syscall traces. Lots of tiny writev calls in the ingress->proxy path, e.g.:
```
writev(fd, iov, 3) = 64
writev(fd, iov, 2) = 45
writev(fd, iov, 1) = 32
```
This syscall churn adds up on high QPS small-request workloads.

matt: I ran a microbench toggling grpc framing coalesce: when writev isn't coalesced median tokenization-only path jumps by ~0.7ms. Consistent with syscall overhead.

anjali: Hmm — did batching heuristics change where we cut frames? We lowered max_frame_size in preparse recently for safety, that could increase fragmentation.

rachel: Config diff from commit abcdef1 shows both the kernel preference and max_frame_size tweak. Perf snapshot correlates with that commit.

perf-bot: Regression alert — host_preparse_cpu +18% vs baseline; syscall rate +12%. Related commit: abcdef1. See /perf/diff/abcdef1 and /perf/snap/1966123456

kai: Options: 1) revert kernel-picker min-batch change (slower rollout), or 2) coalesce writev in the ingress grpc-proxy to reduce syscalls. Which wins short-term?

matt: Coalescing in the proxy is a small, localized change (few lines) and safe. Reverting kernel picker affects model rollout telemetry. Vote to coalesce first.

anjali: +1 to ingress coalescing. I'll put up a PR with canary config and perf test harness. Assigning @matt for review.

rachel: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/proxy/pull/412 — implements writev coalescer and a small buffer window for streaming chunks.

matt: Reviewing now. I'll run a canary and capture perf snapshots (pre/post) and a flamegraph diff.

rachel: If coalesce doesn't restore baseline we'll revert the kernel-picker change as fallback.

kai: Also adding a short-term metric: kvcache_host_preparse_latency_tail to alert if KV cache latency degrades unexpectedly — just in case the memcpy change interacts badly with KV hotspots.

anjali: Added alert rule and a pager threshold at +25% tail.

rachel: Thanks — will update this thread after canary completes. :thumbsup:

matt: Can confirm after initial canary run: host_preparse median restored to ~6.3ms, syscall rate down ~9%. Running larger A/B now.

kai: Nice. Leaving the KV alert in place for 24h.

rachel: Closing for now, reopen if A/B exposes regressions.
